items.text: Card 2's pop is slower (16f, was 10f) and the camera's close-in on it is ~0.9 s longer (it now builds over ~f930–985). Details' slide and the end move ~0.9 s later.
Card 2's header gets the same marker highlight as card 1 while the camera reads it: blue blocks wipe in behind “Slides Left”, then “Page”, and wipe off to the right (~f976–1006).

The flow sits in the middle of the canvas now (it was low: moved up 140px), and in the whole-window view the three frames are closer together (73% spacing, centred). As the camera closes in on the plugin (~f560–604) they spread out to the full spacing, so the links have room for the cards by the time one is dropped.
The pull back from card 2 over to Details is slower (~37f, was ~21f, f1001–1039); Details' slide-in follows it.

New ending: the Figma window slides away to the left (f1094–1130) while the grid fades, leaving the plain ground the film opens on; it holds a beat and the last frame matches frame 0 exactly, so it loops seamlessly. Film is now 1145 frames.

Flicker fixed at the source: the cards had will-change: transform, which let Chrome reuse a stale raster of each card, so a frame looked slightly different depending on what was drawn before it (115 of 126 moments in this span did). Removed: every moment now renders identically, in playback, scrubbing and export.

No Pay ripple and no pull back to the whole step: as card 1's highlight ends (~f780) the camera goes straight across to Sending and down to its bottom (~f780–842), staying close, and the sheet rises there. ~1.7 s shorter; the film is now 1103 frames.

The camera holds on the bottom sheet (~f855–881), then pulls back while panning right toward the second link (f881–912); the dot sets off and card 2 pops in during that move (~f905). Then it closes in on card 2's header (marker highlight ~f952) and goes on to Details (~f977–1015).

The opening's glass panel is now the WebGL liquid-glass material (as in glass-compare): frosted, the rim refracts and lights the names behind it, soft shadow. Same placement, size, fade-in and fade-out as before; the old CSS/SVG glass is kept in the code, switched off.

Right-edge flicker fixed: the back half of each card's rim (in the back's yellow→teal colours) peeked out as a sub-pixel sliver beside the edge and blinked frame to frame. It now wears those colours only while the back faces us (the flip still shows them); with the front facing, the rim is the card's dark edge.
The easing icon (two triangles) is shorter: now about as tall as the ◆ duration icon below it, on both cards.

The ground (grid) and the names are now drawn on a canvas (same layout, motion, flash and blur as before — the SVG still computes them, hidden), and the WebGL glass reads that canvas directly: no per-frame snapshot, so scrubbing the opening shouldn't lag. Looks the same as before (only text anti-aliasing differs).
The hand now grabs the plugin's title bar in the empty stretch between “Motion Card Plugin” and the ×, so it no longer covers the title (the carry and the cursor's path to the easing follow it).
Closer on the plugin while the easing is picked: an extra ~30% zoom builds with the pick (~f560–604) and eases back as the drag sets off, so the drag and drop framing is unchanged.
A bit closer after the drop: the zoom onto the bottom of card 1 (and the pan up to its header that follows) is ~10% tighter (extra zoom 0.95, was 0.77).
The dim behind the bottom sheet now fades in smoothly over the sheet's rise (~f843–861, a gentle in-out curve, starting a touch before the sheet) instead of snapping on with the sheet's fast curve.
A little closer on card 2 too, to match card 1: its close-in is now +62% (was +45%) while its header is read.
The film is now 1920×1200 (16:10), the same as the Zapp and IPL films. Every shot is framed as before, centred, with 60 px more above and below (the aqua grid / Figma canvas extends into it).
